title: The Marshall Plan
subject: histoire
description: In **1947** Europe lay in ruins. The United States offered massive aid to rebuild it, and to hold back communism.

hero.hook: Thirteen billion dollars to save Europe. And, behind the scenes, to win the Cold War.

blocks.text: In June **1947** Europe came out of the war exhausted. Cities destroyed, factories idle, hunger everywhere. In Washington, American Secretary of State **George Marshall** announced an aid plan without precedent.
Officially the point was to rebuild. In reality it was also a strategy: keep poverty from pushing the West toward communism, at a time when **Joseph Stalin** ruled the USSR.
After **1945** the power grids and the railways were broken. The winter of **1946-1947** was brutal and made everything worse: little coal, rationing, anger in the streets.

In France industrial output fell to about **38%** of its **1938** level. Communist parties gained ground at the polls. For the United States, hunger was becoming a political danger: if Europe switched sides through the ballot box, Moscow would win without firing a shot.

blocks.caption: A Marshall Plan poster: American aid presented as a shared European project

blocks.text: To make the plan popular, the Americans ran a poster contest across Europe. More than **10,000** designs came in.

sections.title: The American offer, and the Soviet refusal

blocks.text: On **June 5, 1947**, at Harvard University, Marshall set one clear condition. The Europeans had to agree on a joint plan. No scattered handouts, country by country.

The offer was open to the USSR at first. But Stalin refused, and forbade Poland and Czechoslovakia to accept. Only **16 countries** of Western Europe came together in the **[[OEEC]]**, the body put in charge of sharing out the money. The continent split in two.
Between **1948** and **1952** the United States sent about **13 billion dollars** (more than **150 billion** in today's money). Most of it was not cash: machines, coal, tractors, food.

The system was simple. Europe sold these goods on for local currency. The money raised paid for roads, factories and modernization. By **1952** industrial output stood **35%** above prewar levels. West Germany was beginning its [[Wirtschaftswunder]], the “economic miracle.”
The aid roughly matched Europe's trade deficit: enough for Europe to keep buying American goods without going bankrupt.

sections.title: A political victory as much as an economic one

blocks.text: The plan put the **[[Truman Doctrine]]** into practice: hold Moscow back with prosperity, not only with weapons. It weakened the revolutionary parties, drew the United States and Europe together, and pushed former enemies, France and Germany, to cooperate. That habit of working together prepared the future **[[EEC]]**, the ancestor of the European Union.

events.title: The Harvard speech
events.detail: Marshall announced the principle of coordinated aid.

events.title: Nobel Prize
events.detail: Marshall was honored for building peace through reconstruction.

blocks.text: Between **1948** and **1952** the Marshall Plan poured **13 billion** dollars into Western Europe to rebuild it, slow communism and lay the groundwork for European cooperation.
